explain.say: Imagine you have a robot friend who does exactly what you say, nothing more. You want a jam sandwich. Look at the board: these five steps are an algorithm, which means a list of steps in the right order to get a job done.

faq.a: An algorithm is a list of clear steps, in the right order, that gets a job done. A recipe, the way you brush your teeth and the way a map app finds a route are all algorithms.

faq.q: Why does the order of steps matter?
faq.a: Because each step often needs the one before it. You cannot spread jam until the jar is open, and you cannot put on shoes before socks. Swap two steps and the result can go wrong.
asks: Does the order of instructions matter?
What if steps are in the wrong order?

faq.q: What happens if a step is missing?
faq.a: The job may fail. If you forget to take the bread, the robot has jam but nothing to put it on. Computers cannot guess a missing step, so every step must be written down.
asks: What if I forget a step?
Can a computer guess a missing step?

faq.q: Why do instructions for a computer have to be so exact?
faq.a: A computer does exactly what it is told and cannot guess what you meant. Make a sandwich is too vague; take two slices of bread is clear enough to follow.

faq.q: Where do we use algorithms in real life?
faq.a: Everywhere: recipes for Nigerian jollof rice or Japanese onigiri, directions to school, the rules of a game, and inside every app on a phone.
asks: Examples of algorithms in daily life

facts: The word algorithm comes from the name of al-Khwarizmi, a Persian mathematician who worked in Baghdad in the 800s CE.
A computer program is an algorithm written in a language a computer can follow.

quiz.say: Which of these is an algorithm?

options.show: A list of steps to make tea
options.say: A list of steps to make tea

quiz.why: An algorithm is a set of steps in order that gets a job done, like the steps for making tea.

wrong.1: A cup of tea is the result, not the steps.
wrong.2: A person who likes tea is not a set of instructions.

quiz.say: Your robot spreads jam on the table instead of the bread. What went wrong?
quiz.show: Jam on the table! The problem is…

options.show: A step was not clear or was in the wrong order
options.say: A step was not clear or was in the wrong order

quiz.why: Robots follow steps exactly, so a messy result means a step was missing, unclear or out of order.

wrong.0: Robots do not get lazy; they follow the steps they are given.
wrong.2: The jam is fine; the instructions need fixing.
